questions.question_text: In how many ways can $5$ people be seated in a row if $2$ particular people must sit next to each other?

options.why: Forgot the 2! internal arrangement of the two people inside their block.
Calculated unrestricted 5!, ignoring the restriction that they sit together.
Calculated 3! times 2! instead of arranging 4 units as 4! times 2!.

questions.question_text:
$6$ students line up for lunch.
If Chloe must be at the very front of the line, in how many ways can the $6$ students be arranged?

options.why: Calculated 6!, failing to fix Chloe in the first position.
Calculated 4!, leaving out two students from the arrangement.
Divided 120 by 2 unnecessarily.

questions.solution_text:
Fix Chloe in position $1$ ($1$ choice).
Arrange the remaining $5$ students:
$= 5!$
$= 120$

questions.question_text: In how many ways can $3$ boys and $3$ girls be seated in a row of $6$ chairs if they must alternate genders?

options.why: Counted only one starting gender, omitting the second alternating case.
Calculated 6!, ignoring the alternating gender constraint.
Multiplied 3 by 3 by 2 instead of evaluating factorials 3! times 3! times 2.

questions.question_text: How many $3$-digit even numbers can be formed using the digits $\{1, 3, 5, 6, 8\}$ without repetition?

options.why: Calculated unrestricted 5P3, ignoring the requirement that the number is even.
Counted only 1 even ending digit instead of both 6 and 8.
Multiplied by 4 choices for the last digit instead of 2.

questions.solution_text:
Last digit must be $6$ or $8$ ($2$ choices).
First two digits chosen from remaining $4$: $^{4}P_{2} = 12$.
$= 2 \times 12$
$= 24$

questions.question_text:
$3$ History books and $2$ Geography books are arranged on a shelf.
How many arrangements keep books of the same subject together?

options.why: Forgot the 2! arrangement of the two subject blocks on the shelf.
Calculated 5!, ignoring the requirement to keep subjects together.
Calculated 3! only, omitting the Geography books and subject units.

questions.solution_text:
Arrange $2$ subject units: $2! = 2$.
Internal: History $3! = 6$, Geography $2! = 2$.
$= 2 \times 6 \times 2$
$= 24$

questions.question_text:
$4$ boys and $2$ girls sit in a row.
In how many ways can they sit such that the $2$ girls do NOT sit next to each other?

options.why: Calculated the number of arrangements where the girls DO sit together.
Calculated unrestricted total arrangements 6! without separating girls.
Divided 720 by 2 assuming half of all arrangements separate the girls.

questions.solution_text:
Total arrangements $= 6! = 720$.
Girls together $= 5! \times 2! = 240$.
Girls separated $= 720 - 240 = 480$.

questions.question_text: How many $4$-digit numbers greater than $6000$ can be formed from the digits $\{2, 4, 6, 7, 9\}$ without repeating digits?

options.why: Calculated unrestricted 5! = 120 without restricting the first digit.
Calculated arrangements for only 1 starting digit instead of all 3 valid digits.
Used only 2 starting digits instead of all 3 valid digits (6, 7, 9).

questions.solution_text:
First digit must be $6, 7$, or $9$ ($3$ choices).
Remaining $3$ digits: $^{4}P_{3} = 24$.
$= 3 \times 24$
$= 72$

questions.question_text:
$4$ couples ($8$ people) sit in a row of $8$ seats.
In how many ways can they sit if each couple must sit together?

options.why: Multiplied 4! by 2 instead of 2 to the power 4 for internal couple arrangements.
Calculated 8!, ignoring all couple groupings.
Multiplied by 2 cubed = 8 instead of 2 to the power 4 = 16 for four couples.

questions.solution_text:
Arrange $4$ couple units: $4! = 24$.
Internal couple swaps: $2^4 = 16$.
$= 24 \times 16$
$= 384$
